steps: Step 1 - Write the implementation plan and freeze the baseline (touches: docs/plans/2026-10-18-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-implementation-plan.md; reads docs/index.md, docs/plans/2026-07-13-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-design-plan.md, specs/state.md, specs/acceptance/index.md). Record `git status --short` and run the existing characterization selectors as the baseline: `pytest -q tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py tests/test_resume_command.py -k 'projection and (resume or integrity or call_frame or mutation_order or optional_step_id or schema_boundary)'`. The plan doc lists the decisions this task already fixes: the audit runs in three places (CLI, structural-root executor, reached call); the state schema stays at 2.1; the failure delta is status/error/updated_at. It also records the known current gaps. (a) resume.py persists observability overrides before the checksum check, so the precheck already writes state. (b) calls.py picks the callee with `workflow_import_bundle(loaded_bundle, step['call'])` and picks retry families by `.orc` suffix and `split('::retry::')`. (c) loader.py's `yaml.load(PreservingLoader)` silently collapses duplicate `imports` keys. (d) build.py sets frontend_kind only on the selected entry bundle. (e) fail_run/_write_state go through RunState and can drop unknown root fields. Write the TDD tasks below in this order. Executor and loader must not grow: put new logic in new modules and keep each new module under 500 lines.

Step 2 - Typed Workflow Lisp provenance, item 8 (touches: orchestrator/workflow_lisp/compiler.py, orchestrator/workflow_lisp/workflows.py, orchestrator/workflow_lisp/build.py, orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_build_artifacts.py or a new tests/test_workflow_lisp_frontend_kind.py). First write failing tests through `compile_stage3_entrypoint` and `build_frontend_bundle`. They check that every validated, lowered, and imported Workflow Lisp bundle has `provenance.frontend_kind == 'workflow_lisp'`. They check that a classic-YAML bundle passed via `imported_workflow_bundles` comes back as the same object (`is`) with frontend_kind None. They check that `CallExecutor._is_workflow_lisp_target` is true for a Workflow Lisp bundle (whatever its path suffix) and false for a YAML bundle even when its path ends in `.orc`. Then implement. In compiler.py/workflows.py, set the provenance at the single point where the compiler produces each validated or lowered bundle, using `dataclasses.replace(provenance, frontend_kind='workflow_lisp')`. Skip bundles that came from `imported_workflow_bundles` (identity check), so YAML imports pass through as the same object. In build.py, change `build_frontend_bundle` to keep the selected bundle's frontend_kind instead of overwriting it. In calls.py, `_is_workflow_lisp_target` becomes `getattr(workflow_provenance(b), 'frontend_kind', None) == 'workflow_lisp'`. Run the lexical-checkpoint, observability, and lisp-example selectors that already read frontend_kind (tests/test_workflow_lisp_lexical_checkpoint_default_resume.py, tests/test_runtime_observability.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_examples.py).

Step 3 - Classic-YAML duplicate import-alias detection, item 5 (touches: new orchestrator/loader_imports_scan.py, orchestrator/loader.py, tests/test_loader_validation.py). First write failing tests through `WorkflowLoader.load`, monkeypatching `orchestrator.loader.build_loaded_workflow_bundle` to raise if it is called. Cases: duplicate alias keys inside one `imports`; a `<<` merge inside `imports` that repeats an alias; two direct top-level `imports` sections with a shared alias; top-level `<<` merge sources that each carry `imports`. Each must give exactly one `imports.<alias>: duplicate import alias` naming every `line L, column C` (1-based, at the alias key) and no duplicate-section message. Two sections with distinct aliases (both direct, or one merged and one explicit) must give exactly one `imports: duplicate top-level mapping` naming each `imports` key position. A single merged `imports` with unique aliases must still load. Implement a pure function `scan_import_aliases(text) -> list[str]` in the new module. It walks the node tree from `yaml.compose(text, Loader=PreservingLoader)`: top-level mapping keys, `<<` merge values (one mapping or a sequence of them, and anchors/aliases resolved through the node graph), and `imports` mapping keys including their own `<<` merges. It collects `start_mark.line+1` and `start_mark.column+1` for every alias key and every `imports` key. Report duplicate aliases first, and report a duplicate section only when no alias repeats. In `WorkflowLoader._load_workflow_file` (loader.py around the `yaml.load` call), read the text once, run the scan, `_add_error` each message, and `return {}` before `_load_imports` and `build_loaded_workflow_bundle`, so `load` raises `WorkflowValidationError`.

Step 4 - Projection boundary alias and resume-slot enumeration, item 3 and the state_projection interface (touches: orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py, new orchestrator/workflow/resume_slots.py, the projection builder that constructs `CallBoundaryProjection` (locate with `grep -rn 'CallBoundaryProjection(' orchestrator`, probably orchestrator/workflow/executable_ir.py or lowering.py), tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py). First write failing tests for the following. (a) `CallBoundaryProjection` has a keyword `import_alias`, filled with the authored `call` alias for root and loop-contained boundaries. (b) `ResumeProjectionValidationError(ValueError)` has `.reason` and `.message`, and `str()` equals the message. (c) `enumerate_resume_slots(state)` returns `candidates_by_step_id` (root, finalization (region.value 'finalization'), and loop-local slots carrying `iteration_index`, for every persisted iteration that bookkeeping admits), `call_boundaries_by_step_id` (loop-contained runtime ids built only through `IterationStepKeyProjection.runtime_step_id` and `CallBoundaryProjection.runtime_step_id`), and `unclaimed_explicit_rows` as a snapshotted tuple of (row name, persisted step_id), unhashable ids included. It does not mutate or backfill (deep-copy equality). (d) Every listed unsupported_shape and invalid_loop_progress message for `ProcessItems`/`ReviewLoop`, including the four repeat_until forms: active, condition success, successful exhaustion with a completed loop step, and failed exhaustion whose loop step `error.type` is `repeat_until_iterations_exhausted`. The declared max comes from the projection/step definition. (e) `resolve_resume_step_id(slot_index, step_id, presentation_key=None)` returns `.slot`, `.candidate_count`, `.exact_identity_candidate_count`. An unhashable or malformed id gives count 0 and no exception. (f) `resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id)` returns `.boundary` and `.candidate_count`. Implement the enumeration, loop validation, and result dataclasses in resume_slots.py. state_projection.py gets only the thin methods, the error class, and the field. No string splitting or prefix matching: candidate ids are generated forward from the projection and compared exactly.

Step 5 - Retry-lineage indexing, item 4 lineage rules (touches: new orchestrator/workflow/resume_retry_lineage.py, new tests/test_resume_retry_lineage.py). First write failing tests for `index_retry_lineage(boundary_step_id, frame_items, *, frontend_kind)`. Cases: a base B plus `B::retry::1..n` gives failed_predecessors in ordinal order, at most one running_member, and any number of completed_members. Then the error reasons: ambiguous_resumable_call_frame (two running members, mixed bases, a duplicate ordinal, two non-completed frames on a non-Lisp boundary); unsupported_shape (missing ordinal (gap), malformed `::retry::x` or `::retry::0`, nested `::retry::1::retry::2`, unknown status); missing_call_boundary (call_step_id differs); persisted_import_alias_mismatch (aliases differ). Also check that mapping order never changes the result, and that `next_unused_retry_frame_id` returns the lowest unused positive ordinal across all members (completed included) and is idempotent. Implement `RetryFrameMember(frame_id, ordinal)`, `CallFrameRetryLineage`, `CallFrameRetryLineageError(ValueError).reason`, `index_retry_lineage`, and `next_unused_retry_frame_id`. Parse ordinals with exactly one `rpartition('::retry::')` plus a strict positive-int check on the suffix (`str.isdigit`, no leading zero), and reject any base that still contains the marker. This parsing applies only to frame ids, which the lineage owns; it does not touch step identities.

Step 6 - The scope auditor, items 1, 2, 7 (touches: new orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py, new tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py). First write failing tests through `audit_scope(bundle, state, scope_path)` using generated temporary YAML workflows. Diagnostic tests: one per reason (all twelve), each checking the exact field, offending_value, candidate_count, and call_boundary_step_id from item 7. All seven context keys are always present, with `diagnostic_schema == 'resume_projection_integrity_error.v1'`. scope_path and expected_owner come out right for root and child paths. Container offending values are null, and private values (bound inputs, artifacts, frame state, malformed list contents) never appear anywhere in the serialized diagnostic. Compatibility tests: an absent step_id is accepted for completed, skipped, failed, running-loop and result rows; a present id is always audited; current_step.step_id, call_frames.*.call_step_id and loop selectors are mandatory; the input state is deep-equal before and after. ResumeScopePath tests: frozen, list snapshotted to a tuple, `.root`, `.child`, `.projection_scope`, `.as_context()`. Architecture test: parse the module AST and check that it imports neither `migration_parity` nor `procedure_identity_retirement`, does not reference the four loader/validator names, and contains no `receipt` identifier or string, and no `cache` combined with audit/resume projection/projection integrity. Check also that it never opens files, loads workflows, or calls `calculate_checksum`. Implement ResumeScopePath, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError(ValueError).error, a `_diagnostic(reason, scope_path, bundle, state, field, value, candidate_count, boundary_id)` builder, and `audit_scope`. audit_scope checks the container shapes, calls `projection.enumerate_resume_slots` (mapping ResumeProjectionValidationError onto the diagnostic), resolves each explicit `steps.*.step_id` and `current_step.step_id`, flags unclaimed rows, and for call frames resolves call_step_id with `resolve_call_boundary`, checks the alias against `boundary.import_alias`, checks that `workflow_import_bundle(bundle, boundary.import_alias)` exists (missing_imported_bundle), and groups frames per boundary with `index_retry_lineage`, using the imported bundle's frontend_kind. It does not recurse into child frames on its own: callers recurse with their own selected bundle, so checksum and bound-input ordering stays with calls.py. Re-export `index_retry_lineage`, `next_unused_retry_frame_id`, `CallFrameRetryLineage`, `CallFrameRetryLineageError`, and `RetryFrameMember` from this module. If it exceeds 500 lines, move the call-frame half into resume_projection_integrity_frames.py.

Step 7 - StateManager failure envelopes, item 6 (touches: orchestrator/state.py, tests/test_state_manager.py). First write failing tests. `record_workflow_checksum_mismatch(*, workflow_file, persisted_checksum, current_checksum, reason)` writes exactly `{'type': 'workflow_checksum_mismatch', 'message': 'Workflow has been modified since the run started', 'context': {...four keys}}`, rejects a reason outside the four literals, sets status 'failed', and refreshes updated_at. `record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(error)` stores the given dict unchanged. For both, every other byte of the raw state.json stays the same, including an unknown root key, current_step, steps, call_frames and the rest of the run tree. Neither calls `fail_run` (assert by observable state, not by mock). Implement both under `self._lock`: read the raw JSON, update those three keys, write atomically with the existing temp-file plus os.replace helper used by `_write_state`, then mirror the three fields into `self.state`. Do not round-trip through RunState.to_dict, because it can drop unknown fields.

Step 8 - Resume CLI ordering, items 1 and 6 (touches: orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py, tests/test_resume_command.py). First write failing tests. Monkeypatch `orchestrator.cli.commands.resume.audit_scope` to record calls and check ordering: it runs after the checksum is accepted and before observability override persistence, open_executor_session, write_process_metadata and WorkflowExecutor construction. The existing checksum-precheck failure must now leave the run tree byte-identical even when observability overrides are passed. On an audit failure: exit 1, the reason printed to stderr, and a run-tree diff limited to state.json status/error/updated_at (no session, process metadata, or executor). force_restart skips the audit. Update tests/test_resume_command.py:test_projection_resume_integrity_mutation_order_cli_root_explicit_id_corruption and test_resume_fails_closed_on_projection_current_step_integrity_mismatch to the new contract instead of deleting them. Implement: `from orchestrator.workflow.resume_projection_integrity import audit_scope, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, ResumeScopePath` at module level. Move the `_merge_observability_overrides`/`_write_state` block after the checksum validation, and add the audit right after it in the `not force_restart` branch, calling `audit_scope(workflow_bundle, state.to_dict(), ResumeScopePath.root(state.workflow_file))`. On failure call `state_manager.record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(exc.error)`, print `Error: <message>`, and return 1.

Step 9 - Structural-root executor guard, items 1 and 6 (touches: orchestrator/workflow/executor.py, possibly a new orchestrator/workflow/resume_root_guard.py to keep executor.py from growing, tests/test_resume_command.py or a new tests/test_executor_resume_root_guard.py). First write failing tests through `WorkflowExecutor.execute(resume=True)` with a real StateManager. Cases: the workflow file is modified after the run started; the recorded checksum is missing; state.workflow_file is missing; the workflow file is unreadable or deleted. Each persists the checksum envelope with the matching reason, with status/error/updated_at as the only delta, and never reaches audit_scope (monkeypatch `orchestrator.workflow.executor.audit_scope` as a recorder) or `_execute_prologue` (observe that no bound-input or session bookkeeping is written). A checksum-compatible stale id written after a CLI-equivalent audit gives the projection envelope with the same three-field delta and stops before the prologue. A child call-frame executor never calls the executor-level audit_scope for the root guard. Implement in `execute()` before `_execute_prologue`, guarded by `resume and not isinstance(self.state_manager, _CallFrameStateManager)` (or the existing child marker if one exists). Compute the checksum with `self.state_manager.calculate_checksum(path)` against `state.workflow_file` resolved like `StateManager.validate_checksum`, and map the outcomes to the four reasons. Then call `audit_scope(self.loaded_bundle, state, ResumeScopePath.root(state['workflow_file']))` and return `self.state_manager.load().to_dict()` after recording on failure. In resume.py's `finally`, close the executor session as failed without overwriting state.error: the close must re-read the error, and if the close itself raises, log and keep the diagnostic. Cover this with a test that makes close fail.

Step 10 - Reached-call revalidation, retry lineage and recursion, items 1 and 4 (touches: orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_state.py only if a frame accessor is needed, tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py). First write failing tests through `CallExecutor.execute_call` and the public resume paths, using two-level YAML imports and Workflow Lisp imports via frontend_kind. Ordering, observed by monkeypatching `orchestrator.workflow.calls.audit_scope`: `resolve_call_boundary` is called exactly once per reached identity with positional arguments; the callee bundle comes from `boundary.import_alias`, and a persisted alias mismatch fails closed without redirecting; validation runs after visit/start publication and after authored-input, managed/runtime-input, write-root, checksum and resume-bound-input checks, and before `_CallFrameStateManager` or a child `WorkflowExecutor` is created (spy on both constructors via module attributes). Collisions: a completed frame whose id equals the target frame id (call_step_id matching, stale, or missing) is rejected with `resume_state_invalid_result(..., detail='completed_call_frame_id_collision')`, whose context is exactly the five keys, with no child created and frames unchanged. With a running member: its call_resume_checksum_mismatch or bound-input error wins, then each failed predecessor is checksum-validated and audited in ordinal order, then the member's own scope is audited and resumed. Without a running member: predecessors are validated before allocation via `next_unused_retry_frame_id`. A nested stale id two levels down fails closed, with the scope_path listing both frame ids. Implement in execute_call. Collision check: right after computing frame_id, before grouping. Boundary resolution: `projection.resolve_call_boundary(projection.enumerate_resume_slots(state), step_id)`, replacing the alias lookup. Lineage: replace `_retry_frame_id`, `_retry_family_base` and `_is_failed_retry_family_frame` with `index_retry_lineage`/`next_unused_retry_frame_id`, keeping the existing checksum and bound-input validators and running them in the required order. Child audit: `audit_scope(imported_target, frame_state, parent_scope_path.child(frame_id))`. Thread the parent scope path through the executor, e.g. a `resume_scope_path` attribute set on the child executor, with root as the default. On audit failure, return `{'status': 'failed', 'exit_code': 2, 'error': exc.error, ...}` unchanged. When the child_state error type is `resume_projection_integrity_error`, return it unwrapped instead of `call_failed`, so ancestor frames persist ordinary failed snapshots and promote the same dict.

Step 11 - Sticky, non-routable projection failure and finalization envelope, item 6 (touches: orchestrator/workflow/executor.py (`_handle_control_flow`, the step-result/run-error promotion path, `_finalization_failure_error`, `_execute_epilogue`), orchestrator/workflow/loops.py (`execute_for_each`, `execute_repeat_until`), orchestrator/workflow/finalization.py (`record_step_result`, `continue_into_finalization`), tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py and a new tests/test_resume_projection_sticky_failure.py). First write failing tests with authored `on.success`/`on.failure`/`on.always` gotos, `on_error=continue`, a call inside for_each and repeat_until, and a `finally` block. A reached-call projection error stops the run: `_handle_control_flow` returns '_stop', no next iteration runs, and the run error equals the diagnostic. Finalization still runs. A cleanup failure records `finalization.status == 'failed'` and `finalization.failure == {'step', 'step_id', 'error': None or the projection error}`, and leaves the run error as the original diagnostic. A projection error raised only inside finalization becomes both the run error and `finalization.failure.error`. Epilogue and session close preserve it. Implement one predicate `is_projection_integrity_error(result)` in resume_projection_integrity.py and check it first in `_handle_control_flow` (before cycle-guard and goto handling), in the loop executors' continuation checks, and in finalization/epilogue error selection, so `finalization_failed` never replaces it.

Step 12 - Forensic current_step in observability, item 6 (touches: orchestrator/observability/report.py (`build_status_snapshot`, `render_status_markdown`), orchestrator/monitor/classifier.py (`_active_cursor_heartbeat`), orchestrator/monitor/messages.py (`_heartbeat_at`), orchestrator/dashboard/cursor.py if it drives stalled detection, tests/test_observability_report.py and the monitor tests). First write failing tests on a failed state whose error type is `resume_projection_integrity_error` or `workflow_checksum_mismatch` and whose current_step is unchanged. The snapshot shows the run failed with the error. That step has status and summary 'pending', `current_visit_count` None, and is counted under pending, not running. The markdown never says 'in progress' for it. Heartbeat and stalled classification ignore it. Implement one shared helper (e.g. `is_forensic_current_step(state)` in orchestrator/observability/report.py, imported by the monitor modules) and use it where `current_step` is treated as live.

Step 13 - Specs and acceptance (touches: specs/state.md, specs/acceptance/index.md, docs/capability_status_matrix.md (status row), docs/index.md only if routing changes). Add a 'Checksum-Compatible Resume Projection Integrity' section to specs/state.md covering: audit placement (CLI, structural-root executor, reached call); explicit-identity versus omission compatibility; loop progress forms; call-frame lineage and retry allocation; the collision contract; the YAML import-alias diagnostics; both failure envelopes and their three-field delta; sticky non-routability and the finalization.failure shape; forensic current_step reporting; the diagnostic schema with its twelve reasons and privacy rules; the absence of receipts, caches and migrations; schema 2.1 unchanged. Add numbered acceptance entries to specs/acceptance/index.md mapping each clause to its test module from steps 2-12.

Step 14 - Verification (no new files). Run `pytest --collect-only -q` on every added or renamed test module: tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py, tests/test_resume_retry_lineage.py, tests/test_resume_projection_sticky_failure.py, and any executor-guard or frontend_kind modules. Run the narrow selectors, then `pytest -q tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py tests/test_resume_command.py tests/test_state_manager.py tests/test_loader_validation.py tests/test_observability_report.py tests/test_runtime_observability.py tests/test_workflow_lisp_lexical_checkpoint_default_resume.py tests/test_at68_resume_force_restart.py tests/test_adjudicated_provider_resume.py`, then the full suite. Run one end-to-end orchestrator smoke check: run a small imported-call example from workflows/examples to an interrupted state, corrupt one explicit step_id while leaving the checksum unchanged, and run `python -m orchestrator resume <run_id>`. Expect exit 1, the stable diagnostic on stderr, and a state.json delta limited to status/error/updated_at. Check that new modules are under 500 lines (`wc -l`) and that no function exceeds complexity 12 (project linter). Commit after each green step with the required Co-Authored-By trailer. Do not use `--no-verify` and do not create worktrees.

findings: [P0] The plan has no available governing target contract. The checkout has docs/plans/2026-07-13-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-design-plan.md, but neither its promised accepted design (docs/design/resume_projection_integrity_hardening.md) nor its promised implementation plan exists. Steps 4-7 refer to 'every listed' loop shape, twelve diagnostic reasons, seven context keys, and four checksum reasons without defining them. Step 1 must first establish and review those decisions against the normative specs; otherwise implementers must invent behavior and Step 13 can silently expand the intended scope.

[P0] The promised three-field-only failure delta is incompatible with Steps 10-11. A reached-call audit occurs after the parent visit/start and loop-progress writes; execute_call then persists child and ancestor failed snapshots, and finalization can write steps, finalization state, sidecars, and workflow effects. Existing _CallFrameStateManager._persist and FinalizationController.record_step_result confirm those writes. A stale nested identity therefore cannot leave only root status/error/updated_at changed. Either preflight every persisted descendant before any resumed effect and define how cleanup is excluded, or explicitly narrow the delta contract; the current plan cannot satisfy the stated intended change.

[P1] Auditing state.to_dict() after StateManager.load() misses or crashes on the malformed persisted shapes the plan promises to diagnose. RunState.from_dict indexes required keys directly and builds each for_each entry with ForEachState(**state_dict), so a missing workflow_file, non-mapping for_each, or malformed loop entry fails before audit_scope. It also discards unknown root fields. Route the raw persisted JSON through a tolerant shape audit before typed conversion, or change the loader contract and cover CLI/direct-executor cases for these shapes.

[P1] The proposed retry parser rejects valid nested Workflow Lisp call frames. CallExecutor.frame_id_with_overrides prefixes a child frame ID with its parent frame ID; when the parent is B::retry::1, the child's base itself contains ::retry::. Step 5's single rpartition plus 'reject any base that still contains the marker' treats that inherited marker as a malformed child retry. Add a two-level test with a child under a retried parent and scope the retry suffix to the child's own frame identity.

[P1] Step 6 groups call frames per call boundary, while Step 5 rejects mixed retry bases. One authored call boundary can have several legitimate visits (call_step_id::visit::1, ::visit::2), and nested/loop executions add more families. Group and validate by an explicit visit/frame family within the resolved boundary; otherwise an ordinary repeat visit is misreported as ambiguous_resumable_call_frame.

[P1] The checksum and write ordering is not closed at the CLI. resume_workflow loads the workflow before validate_checksum; for .orc, build_frontend_bundle creates .orchestrate/build artifacts, and a missing/unreadable workflow or compile failure returns before either the proposed checksum envelope or projection audit. Step 8 moves observability persistence but leaves this path, while Step 9 covers only direct executor entry. Specify and test the CLI's checksum error precedence and run-tree effects, including absent workflow_file and unreadable source; do not claim one envelope for cases that return plain load errors.

[P1] The failure writer/finally design does not preserve the stated persisted delta. Re-reading raw JSON then dumping it with the existing JSON writer preserves values but not every other byte if the original formatting differs. More seriously, resume.py's finally still calls close_executor_session and StateManager._write_state(), whose RunState.to_dict drops unknown root fields and changes runtime_observability. Re-reading state.error alone does not fix either issue. Tests must assert the full run tree and unknown-root retention after executor-guard failures and close failures, and the writer must patch the raw representation or the contract must be defined as a semantic field delta.

[P2] Several execution instructions do not match this checkout's entry points and test policy. Step 3 names WorkflowLoader._load_workflow_file, but the yaml.load boundary is _load_workflow. Step 14 says 'full suite' without the repository-required pytest -q -n 16 --dist=worksteal in tmux after narrow selectors. Correct the symbol and put the exact broad command and tmux gate in the plan so execution does not stop at narrower verification.

steps: Step 1 - Write the governing target contract and implementation plan, then gate them with an independent review, before any runtime change (touches: specs/state.md (new section 'Checksum-Compatible Resume Projection Integrity'), specs/acceptance/index.md (numbered entries, each marked pending and naming its planned test module), new docs/design/resume_projection_integrity_hardening.md (the accepted target design promised by docs/plans/2026-07-13-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-design-plan.md), new docs/plans/2026-10-18-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-implementation-plan.md; reads docs/index.md, docs/templates/design_template.md, the 2026-07-13 design plan, specs/state.md, specs/acceptance/index.md, docs/capability_status_matrix.md). Finding [P0] says the checkout has no target contract, so this step writes it out in full from the task statement, and later steps cite these sections instead of saying 'every listed'. The spec section must contain: (a) the seven context keys (`diagnostic_schema`='resume_projection_integrity_error.v1', `reason`, `scope_path`, `field`, `offending_value`, `expected_owner`={workflow_file, workflow_checksum, projection_scope}, `candidate_count`, `call_boundary_step_id`), all always present, plus the message template 'Resume projection integrity audit failed: <reason>'; (b) a table of the twelve reasons (unknown_explicit_step_id, presentation_slot_mismatch, out_of_scope_step_id, unclaimed_explicit_step_row, missing_required_identity, missing_call_boundary, ambiguous_call_boundary, ambiguous_resumable_call_frame, persisted_import_alias_mismatch, missing_imported_bundle, unsupported_shape, invalid_loop_progress), each with its exact field, offending_value and candidate_count from task item 7; (c) the privacy rules; (d) the four checksum reasons (workflow_modified, missing_recorded_checksum, missing_workflow_path, workflow_unavailable) and the checksum envelope {type 'workflow_checksum_mismatch', message 'Workflow has been modified since the run started', context {workflow_file, persisted_checksum, current_checksum, reason}}; (e) the for_each rules, the four repeat_until progress forms, and the exact ResumeProjectionValidationError reason/message pairs from the interface list (eight unsupported_shape and ten invalid_loop_progress messages, given for ProcessItems/ReviewLoop); (f) the YAML import diagnostics; (g) the failure-envelope classes in the step-1 decisions below; (h) retry-lineage and frame-family rules; (i) sticky non-routability and the finalization.failure shape; (j) forensic current_step reporting; (k) no receipts, caches or migrations, and schema 2.1 unchanged. The design doc records these decisions, each with what it makes harder later: (1) Failure-envelope classes, replacing the single 'three-field delta' claim (finding [P0]). ROOT class: CLI audit failure, executor checksum failure, executor root-audit failure. The persisted delta is root status/error/updated_at only, and nothing has executed yet. REACHED-CALL class: a nested or call-frame audit failure that happens after the parent's ordinary visit/start publication. The allowed writes are the caller's ordinary visit/start/loop-progress publication, the caller's failed call-step result and current/visit snapshot, each ancestor frame's ordinary failed snapshot, the root status/error, and any configured finalization (its steps, finalization state, sidecars and effects). The selected callee frame and its state directory stay unchanged, and no callee effect runs. A stale nested identity therefore produces REACHED-CALL writes, not a three-field delta. The root audit does not recurse into frame state, because the task assigns nested scopes to the reached call. (2) 'Persisted delta' is defined on parsed JSON: the parsed state.json equals the original except the allowed keys, with key order and unknown root fields preserved. Byte identity is required only where nothing is written (checksum precheck, plain load errors). (3) The audit takes the raw persisted JSON mapping, never `RunState.to_dict()`. (4) Frame families: a family is grouped within one resolved boundary, per visit (details in Step 5). (5) CLI ordering: checksum before bundle load (details in Step 8). Step 1 also characterizes and records the current gaps, each with a file:line reference: (a) resume.py persists observability overrides (around line 390-406) before the checksum check at line 466, and it loads or builds the bundle before checksum validation; (b) calls.py selects the callee with `workflow_import_bundle(self.executor.loaded_bundle, call_alias)` and groups retries with `_retry_family_base`'s `split('::retry::', 1)` and the `.orc`-based `_is_workflow_lisp_target`; (c) loader.py `_load_workflow` (line ~177 `yaml.load(f, Loader=PreservingLoader)`) silently collapses duplicate `imports` keys; (d) build.py sets frontend_kind only on the selected bundle; (e) `RunState.from_dict` indexes required keys directly and calls `ForEachState(**state_dict)`, and `_write_state`/`fail_run` round-trip through `RunState.to_dict`, which drops unknown root fields; (f) the resume.py `finally` calls `close_executor_session` and then `_write_state()`; (g) where `_load_resume_workflow_bundle`/`FrontendBuildRequest` writes build artifacts (expected: the workspace `.orchestrate/build`, outside the run tree; confirm it). Record `git status --short` and run the baseline: `pytest -q tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py tests/test_resume_command.py -k 'projection and (resume or integrity or call_frame or mutation_order or optional_step_id or schema_boundary)'`. Gate: dispatch a quality-reviewer subagent to review the spec section, design doc and plan against the existing normative text of specs/state.md and the task statement. List every conflict or interpretation in the plan doc under 'Assumptions/Conflicts'. Two must be listed: the per-visit-family reading of task item 4's 'one retry lineage per boundary', and the narrowed delta classes. Do not start Step 2 until the review has no unresolved blocking item. Step 13 may only reconcile docs with this contract; it may not add behavior. Executor and loader must not grow: new logic goes in new modules of under 500 lines each.

Step 2 - Typed Workflow Lisp provenance, item 8 (touches: orchestrator/workflow_lisp/compiler.py, orchestrator/workflow_lisp/workflows.py, orchestrator/workflow_lisp/build.py, orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, new tests/test_workflow_lisp_frontend_kind.py). First write failing tests through `compile_stage3_entrypoint` and `build_frontend_bundle`. They check: every validated, lowered and imported Workflow Lisp bundle has `provenance.frontend_kind == 'workflow_lisp'`; a classic-YAML bundle passed via `imported_workflow_bundles` comes back as the same object (`is`) with frontend_kind None; `build_frontend_bundle` keeps the compiler-set frontend_kind; `CallExecutor._is_workflow_lisp_target` is true for a Workflow Lisp bundle whatever its path suffix, and false for a YAML bundle even when its path ends in `.orc`. Then implement. Set the provenance with `dataclasses.replace(provenance, frontend_kind='workflow_lisp')` at the single point where the compiler produces each validated or lowered bundle. Skip bundles that came from `imported_workflow_bundles` (identity check), so YAML imports pass through as the same object. In build.py, keep the selected bundle's frontend_kind instead of overwriting it. In calls.py, `_is_workflow_lisp_target` becomes `getattr(workflow_provenance(b), 'frontend_kind', None) == 'workflow_lisp'`. Run `pytest --collect-only -q tests/test_workflow_lisp_frontend_kind.py`, the new module, and the existing frontend_kind readers: tests/test_workflow_lisp_lexical_checkpoint_default_resume.py, tests/test_runtime_observability.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_examples.py. Commit when green.

Step 3 - Classic-YAML duplicate import-alias detection, item 5 (touches: new orchestrator/loader_imports_scan.py, orchestrator/loader.py, tests/test_loader_validation.py). First write failing tests through `WorkflowLoader.load`, monkeypatching `orchestrator.loader.build_loaded_workflow_bundle` to raise if it is called. Cases: duplicate alias keys inside one `imports`; a `<<` merge inside `imports` that repeats an alias; two direct top-level `imports` sections with a shared alias; top-level `<<` merge sources that each carry `imports`. Each must give exactly one `imports.<alias>: duplicate import alias` naming every `line L, column C` (1-based, at the alias key) and no duplicate-section message. Two sections with distinct aliases (both direct, or one merged and one explicit) must give exactly one `imports: duplicate top-level mapping` naming each `imports` key position. A single merged `imports` with unique aliases must still load. Implement a pure `scan_import_aliases(text) -> list[str]` in the new module over `yaml.compose(text, Loader=PreservingLoader)`. It walks top-level mapping keys, `<<` merge values (one mapping or a sequence of them; anchors are resolved through the node graph), and `imports` mapping keys including their own `<<` merges. It records `start_mark.line+1` and `start_mark.column+1` for every alias key and every `imports` key. It reports duplicate aliases first, and a duplicate section only when no alias repeats. Hook it into `WorkflowLoader._load_workflow` (the method that holds the `yaml.load(f, Loader=PreservingLoader)` call, loader.py around line 177; the old plan named a nonexistent `_load_workflow_file`). Read the text once, run the scan, `_add_error` each message, and return before `_load_imports` and `build_loaded_workflow_bundle` run, so `load` raises `WorkflowValidationError`. The existing parse must use the same text; do not re-read the file. Run `pytest -q tests/test_loader_validation.py` and commit.

Step 4 - Projection boundary alias and resume-slot enumeration, item 3 and the state_projection interface (touches: orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py, new orchestrator/workflow/resume_slots.py, the builder of `CallBoundaryProjection` (locate with `grep -rn 'CallBoundaryProjection(' orchestrator`), tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py). First write failing tests for the following. (a) `CallBoundaryProjection` has the keyword `import_alias`, filled with the authored `call` alias for root and loop-contained boundaries. (b) `ResumeProjectionValidationError(ValueError)` has `.reason` and `.message`, and `str()` equals the message. (c) `enumerate_resume_slots(state)` takes a raw state mapping and returns: `candidates_by_step_id` (root and finalization slots (region.value 'finalization'), and loop-local slots carrying `iteration_index` for each iteration the bookkeeping admits); `call_boundaries_by_step_id` (loop-contained runtime ids built only through `IterationStepKeyProjection.runtime_step_id` and `CallBoundaryProjection.runtime_step_id`); and `unclaimed_explicit_rows` as a snapshotted tuple of (row name, persisted step_id), unhashable ids included. It does not mutate or backfill (deep-copy equality). (d) A parametrized test of every reason/message pair written into the spec in Step 1(e) (eight unsupported_shape and ten invalid_loop_progress for ProcessItems/ReviewLoop), plus accepted examples of the four repeat_until forms. The declared max comes from the projection's step definition. Inputs that `RunState.from_dict` could not build are included: a non-mapping `for_each`, a non-list `items`, a boolean `current_index`. (e) `resolve_resume_step_id(slot_index, step_id, presentation_key=None)` returns `.slot`, `.candidate_count` and `.exact_identity_candidate_count`; an unhashable or malformed id gives count 0 and no exception. (f) `resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id)` returns `.boundary` and `.candidate_count`. Implement the enumeration, loop validation and result dataclasses in resume_slots.py. state_projection.py gets only the thin methods, the error class and the field. No string splitting or prefix matching on step ids: candidates are generated forward from the projection and compared exactly. Run collect-only and `pytest -q tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py`, then commit.

Step 5 - Retry-lineage indexing and frame families, item 4 lineage rules (touches: new orchestrator/workflow/resume_retry_lineage.py, new tests/test_resume_retry_lineage.py). Frame-id facts from this checkout: `CallExecutor.frame_id_with_overrides` builds `<step_id>::visit::<n>` and prefixes the parent frame id (`<parent_frame_id>.<local>`) for nested frames. Nested frames live in the parent frame's own `call_frames`. So a frame base can legitimately contain an inherited `::retry::` from a retried parent, for example `P::visit::1::retry::1.C::visit::1` (finding [P1]). Rule: the lineage parses only the frame's own trailing suffix, the text after the last `::visit::`. That tail must be `<n>` (the base, ordinal 0) or `<n>::retry::<k>`, where n and k are ASCII digits with no leading zero and k >= 1. Anything else in the own tail is unsupported_shape: `::retry::0`, `::retry::x`, a nested own marker `<n>::retry::1::retry::2`, a missing `::visit::`. Text before the last `::visit::` is never inspected for markers. The family key is the frame id with its own retry suffix removed. This parsing applies only to frame ids, which the lineage owns, never to step identities. First write failing tests for `index_retry_lineage(boundary_step_id, frame_items, *, frontend_kind)`. A base plus `::retry::1..n` gives failed_predecessors in ordinal order, at most one running_member, and any number of completed_members. A child frame under a retried parent (`P::visit::1::retry::1.C::visit::1` with retry `...C::visit::1::retry::1`) indexes as a valid family whose base keeps the inherited marker. Error cases: ambiguous_resumable_call_frame (two running members, mixed family keys passed together, a duplicate ordinal, two non-completed frames on a non-Lisp boundary); unsupported_shape (an ordinal gap, the malformed own tails above, an unknown status); missing_call_boundary (a differing call_step_id); persisted_import_alias_mismatch (differing aliases). Mapping order never changes the result. `next_unused_retry_frame_id` returns the lowest unused positive ordinal across all members, completed included, and is idempotent. Also implement and test `group_frame_families(frame_items) -> dict[family_key, list]` for callers (finding [P1] on visits). It groups one boundary's frames by family key, so `S::visit::1` (failed) and `S::visit::2` (running) are two families, not mixed bases. The cross-family rule is: at most one running member per boundary per parent scope (otherwise ambiguous_resumable_call_frame, with field `call_frames` and count = number of running members); failed frames of other visit families are historical (shape, caller and alias are validated, they are not resumed); a non-Lisp boundary has at most one non-completed frame per family. Record this per-family reading as the Step 1 interpretation. Run collect-only and the module, then commit.

Step 6 - The scope auditor, items 1, 2 and 7 (touches: new orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py, possibly new orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity_frames.py, new tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py). The auditor takes the raw persisted state mapping (finding [P1]): callers pass the JSON dict read from state.json, never `RunState.to_dict()`. It must therefore diagnose, without crashing, a missing or non-string `workflow_file`/`workflow_checksum` used in expected_owner (reported as JSON null), non-mapping `steps`/`call_frames`/`for_each`/`repeat_until`, malformed loop entries, malformed step rows, and non-mapping frames. First write failing tests through `audit_scope(bundle, state, scope_path)` using generated temporary YAML workflows. One test per reason (all twelve) asserts the exact field, offending_value, candidate_count and call_boundary_step_id from the Step 1 table. All seven keys are always present. scope_path and expected_owner are right for root and child paths. Container offending values are null. Private values (bound inputs, artifacts, frame state, the contents of malformed lists or mappings) never appear in `json.dumps(diagnostic)`. Compatibility tests: an absent step_id is accepted for completed, skipped, failed, running-loop and result rows; a present id is always audited; current_step.step_id, call_frames.*.call_step_id, the frame's current position and loop selectors are mandatory; the input is deep-equal before and after. Family tests: a failed `S::visit::1` plus a running `S::visit::2` passes; two running visits fail with ambiguous_resumable_call_frame. ResumeScopePath tests: frozen, list snapshotted to a tuple, `.root`, `.child`, `.projection_scope`, `.as_context()`. Architecture test (AST): no import of `migration_parity` or `procedure_identity_retirement`; none of the four forbidden names; no `receipt`; no `cache` combined with audit, resume projection or projection integrity; no `open`, no workflow loading, no `calculate_checksum`. Implement ResumeScopePath, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError(ValueError) with `.error`, a `_diagnostic(...)` builder, `is_projection_integrity_error(result_or_error)`, and `audit_scope`. audit_scope works in this order: container shapes; `projection.enumerate_resume_slots` (ResumeProjectionValidationError is mapped to the diagnostic); each explicit `steps.*.step_id` and `current_step.step_id`; unclaimed rows. For call frames it calls `resolve_call_boundary` once per frame identity, checks the alias against `boundary.import_alias`, checks that `workflow_import_bundle(bundle, boundary.import_alias)` exists (otherwise missing_imported_bundle), then uses `group_frame_families` plus `index_retry_lineage` per family with the imported bundle's frontend_kind, and applies the cross-family running rule. It does not recurse into frame state; callers recurse with their own selected bundle, so checksum and bound-input ordering stays with calls.py. Re-export the lineage names. If the module exceeds 500 lines, move the call-frame half into resume_projection_integrity_frames.py. Run collect-only and the module, then commit.

Step 7 - StateManager raw-state read and failure writers, item 6 (touches: orchestrator/state.py, tests/test_state_manager.py). This addresses finding [P1] on the writers and on typed conversion. Add three pieces. `read_persisted_state() -> dict`: under `self._lock`, json-load state.json with no RunState conversion, so callers can audit raw shapes that `RunState.from_dict` would reject. `_patch_persisted_state(updates: Mapping[str, Any])`: under the lock, json-load the raw file, assign only the given top-level keys (existing key order kept, new keys appended), write with the same temp-file plus `os.replace` and `indent=2` used by `_write_state`, and mirror the keys onto `self.state` when it is loaded, using no `to_dict`. The two public writers: `record_workflow_checksum_mismatch(*, workflow_file, persisted_checksum, current_checksum, reason)` validates the reason against the four literals (ValueError otherwise) and that the first three values are str or None, then patches status='failed', error=<envelope>, updated_at=<now>. `record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(error)` patches the same three keys with the given dict unchanged. First write failing tests. Write a state.json containing an unknown root key, a malformed `for_each` (non-mapping), current_step, steps, call_frames and runtime_observability. Assert the parsed JSON after each writer equals the parsed original except status/error/updated_at (the semantic delta defined in Step 1(2); byte formatting is not part of the contract), and that key order and the unknown root key are retained. A malformed for_each does not stop the writer, because it never calls `RunState.from_dict`. Neither writer calls `fail_run`; show this by observable state only (no `fail_run` side effects such as step or current_step changes), not with a mock. Run the module and commit.

Step 8 - Resume CLI ordering and envelopes, items 1 and 6 (touches: orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py, tests/test_resume_command.py). This closes finding [P1] on CLI checksum ordering with this order for the non-force_restart path: read the raw state via `state_manager.read_persisted_state()` (missing file or bad JSON keeps the existing load/repair errors) -> schema_version check on the raw dict -> quarantine check -> `workflow_file` present (existing plain 'No workflow file recorded' error, exit 1, nothing written) -> workflow path resolves (existing plain 'Workflow file not found' error, exit 1, nothing written) -> `state_manager.validate_checksum(path)`, moved before bundle load/build (existing message, exit 1, nothing written; an unreadable source maps to the same plain checksum failure, never an envelope) -> `_load_resume_workflow_bundle` (its compile/validation errors keep their current exit codes and plain output; frontend build output goes to the workspace build directory outside the run tree, confirmed in Step 1(g)) -> lowering-schema check -> `audit_scope(workflow_bundle, raw_state, ResumeScopePath.root(raw_state['workflow_file']))` -> only then the typed `state_manager.load()`, observability override persistence, `open_executor_session`, `write_process_metadata` and WorkflowExecutor construction. The CLI never writes the checksum envelope; it belongs only to the structural-root executor (task item 6, first bullet). Typed `RunState.from_dict` failures that the audit already diagnoses cannot occur before the audit, because the audit runs on the raw dict. force_restart skips checksum and audit, as today, and still loads typed state. First write failing tests, monkeypatching `orchestrator.cli.commands.resume.audit_scope` as a recorder and spying on the session, metadata and executor constructors through module attributes. Cases: (1) audit order relative to checksum acceptance and the four later actions; (2) checksum precheck failure with observability overrides passed leaves the run tree byte-identical (nothing is written) and never calls the bundle loader (spy on `_load_resume_workflow_bundle`); (3) absent workflow_file and a missing source file each give the plain error with a byte-identical run tree; (4) an audit failure on a raw state with a non-mapping `for_each`, an unknown root key or a stale explicit id gives exit 1, `Error: Resume projection integrity audit failed: <reason>` on stderr, a run tree whose only change is state.json, and a parsed state.json delta of status/error/updated_at with the unknown key retained, with no session, process metadata or executor; (5) force_restart skips the audit. Update test_projection_resume_integrity_mutation_order_cli_root_explicit_id_corruption and test_resume_fails_closed_on_projection_current_step_integrity_mismatch to the new contract instead of deleting them. Implement with module-level `from orchestrator.workflow.resume_projection_integrity import audit_scope, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, ResumeScopePath`, and record failures with `state_manager.record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(exc.error)`. Run the module and `tests/test_at68_resume_force_restart.py`, then commit.

Step 9 - Structural-root executor guard and failure-safe session close, items 1 and 6 (touches: orchestrator/workflow/executor.py (one call site only), new orchestrator/workflow/resume_root_guard.py, orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py (`finally` block), new tests/test_executor_resume_root_guard.py). Implement `run_root_resume_guard(executor) -> Optional[dict]` in resume_root_guard.py. In `WorkflowExecutor.execute()`, call it immediately before `_execute_prologue` only when `resume` is true and the state manager is not a `CallFrameStateManager`; a non-None return ends execute with that state. The guard: read `raw = state_manager.read_persisted_state()` (never the typed state, per finding [P1]). Missing or non-string `workflow_file` gives missing_workflow_path. Missing `workflow_checksum` gives missing_recorded_checksum. The path is resolved like `StateManager.validate_checksum`; an absent or unreadable file (OSError from `state_manager.calculate_checksum`) gives workflow_unavailable; a differing checksum gives workflow_modified. On a checksum failure it calls `record_workflow_checksum_mismatch` and stops before the audit. Otherwise it runs `orchestrator.workflow.executor.audit_scope(executor.loaded_bundle, raw, ResumeScopePath.root(raw['workflow_file']))` (module-level name in executor.py, passed in or looked up at call time so substitution works); on failure it records the projection envelope. Either failure returns the patched raw state (re-read) and never reaches the prologue. Fix the `finally` (finding [P1]): after a guard failure the CLI must not call `state_manager._write_state()`, because it round-trips RunState and drops unknown root fields. Instead compute the closed session record with `close_executor_session(state_manager.state, ..., status='failed')` and persist only `runtime_observability` through `_patch_persisted_state`, wrapped so that an exception from the close is logged and the persisted diagnostic stays. The success path keeps its existing close plus `_write_state`. First write failing tests through `WorkflowExecutor.execute(resume=True)` with a real StateManager. Cases: modified file, missing recorded checksum, missing workflow_file, deleted file, unreadable file. Each persists the envelope with the matching reason, the parsed delta is status/error/updated_at only, and an unknown root key is retained. The recorder for `orchestrator.workflow.executor.audit_scope` is not called, and the prologue is not reached (no bound-input or prologue bookkeeping written). A checksum-compatible stale id written after a CLI-equivalent audit passed gives the projection envelope with the same delta and stops before the prologue. A child call-frame executor never calls the executor-level audit. A direct executor resume over a raw state with a non-mapping `for_each` is diagnosed rather than crashing. Through `resume_workflow` with the CLI audit substituted to pass: the executor-guard failure keeps the opened session/process metadata, the run-tree diff equals the parsed delta plus the session close in runtime_observability, the unknown root key is retained, and a `close_executor_session` that raises (fault injection) leaves the diagnostic and unknown key intact. Run the new module, tests/test_resume_command.py and tests/test_runtime_observability.py, then commit.

Step 10 - Reached-call revalidation, families, retry lineage and recursion, items 1 and 4 (touches: orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_state.py only if a frame accessor is needed, tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py; if calls.py grows, put the new resume-validation sequence in new orchestrator/workflow/call_resume_validation.py). Delta contract: the Step 1 REACHED-CALL class, not three fields. Tests assert that the selected callee frame entry and its `call_frames/<token>` directory are unchanged, that no callee effect ran, and that the caller and ancestor writes are only the listed ordinary snapshots. First write failing tests through `CallExecutor.execute_call` and the public resume paths, using two-level YAML imports and Workflow Lisp imports (marked by frontend_kind). Ordering, observed by monkeypatching `orchestrator.workflow.calls.audit_scope` and spying on `CallFrameStateManager` and `WorkflowExecutor` constructors through calls.py module attributes: `resolve_call_boundary` is called exactly once per reached identity with positional arguments; the callee bundle comes from `boundary.import_alias`; a persisted alias mismatch fails closed without redirecting; validation runs after visit/start publication and after authored-input, managed/runtime-input, write-root, checksum and resume-bound-input checks, and before any child manager or executor exists. Collision: a completed frame whose id equals the target frame id (call_step_id matching, stale or missing) is rejected with `resume_state_invalid_result(..., detail='completed_call_frame_id_collision')`, whose context is exactly the five keys; no child is created and the frames are unchanged. Families: a failed `S::visit::1` plus a reached visit 2 allocates or resumes only within the visit-2 family. A nested child under a retried parent (`P::visit::1::retry::1.C::visit::1`) resumes, and its retry allocation yields `...C::visit::1::retry::1`. With a running member: its call_resume_checksum_mismatch or bound-input error wins; then each failed predecessor is checksum-validated and audited in ordinal order; then the member's own scope is audited and resumed. Without a running member: predecessors are validated before allocation via `next_unused_retry_frame_id`. A nested stale id two levels down fails closed with scope_path listing both frame ids, and the same diagnostic reaches the root unwrapped (not `call_failed`). Implement in this order. Compute the target frame id with the non-resume branch of `frame_id_with_overrides`. The resume short-circuit that returns the first non-completed frame with a matching call_step_id must be replaced, because it selects by mapping order. Then run the collision check. Then resolve the boundary with `projection.resolve_call_boundary(projection.enumerate_resume_slots(state), step_id)`, replacing the alias lookup. Then index the family with `group_frame_families`/`index_retry_lineage`, which replaces `_retry_frame_id`, `_retry_family_base` and `_is_failed_retry_family_frame`; the write-root collision loop uses the lineage membership instead of `_is_failed_retry_family_frame`. Keep the existing checksum and bound-input validators, run in the required order. Child audit: `audit_scope(imported_target, frame_state, parent_scope_path.child(frame_id))`, with the scope path threaded through a `resume_scope_path` attribute on the child executor (root by default). On audit failure return `{'status': 'failed', 'exit_code': 2, 'error': exc.error, ...}` unchanged. When a child_state error passes `is_projection_integrity_error`, return it unwrapped. Run the module and tests/test_adjudicated_provider_resume.py, then commit.

- Step 6: new workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py plus _frames.py (audit_scope, ResumeScopePath, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, all twelve reasons, privacy, no mutation, source-constraint test).
- Step 7: StateManager.read_persisted_state, _patch_persisted_state and the two failure writers. They patch only status/error/updated_at on the raw JSON, so unknown root fields survive. validate_checksum now falls back to the raw checksum when no typed state is loaded.
- Step 8: resume CLI order is now raw read, schema and quarantine gates, workflow file checks, checksum precheck, bundle load, lowering-schema check, audit_scope, and only then typed load, overrides, session, metadata and executor. Failures persist only the envelope.
- Step 9: new workflow/resume_root_guard.py, called once at the top of WorkflowExecutor.execute(resume=True) before the typed load. It gives the four checksum reasons plus the root audit. The CLI session open/close now patches only runtime_observability, and a failing close is logged and cannot replace the diagnostic.
- Step 10: new workflow/call_resume_validation.py and a rewritten CallExecutor.execute_call. In resume mode it does one resolve_call_boundary per reached identity and selects the callee by the boundary alias. It rejects a completed-frame id collision with the exact five-key context. It indexes retry lineage and checks running-member checksum and bound inputs first. Then it checks failed predecessors in ordinal order, then audits the running member's scope, all before any child manager or executor is built. Diagnostics return unwrapped, and the child executor carries resume_scope_path.
- Step 11: _handle_control_flow stops first on a projection error and promotes it to the run error. Loops stop with the unwrapped error and no next iteration. A finalization failure is supplemental: finalization.failure.error is null for an ordinary failure, and a projection error arising only in finalization becomes the run error. It is never replaced.

DECISIONS AND ALTERNATIVES
- Frame selection on resume: the plan said to compute the target frame id with the non-resume branch and group per visit. That failed on real resumes because re-entering a call bumps the visit counter, so the interrupted frame S::visit::1 is looked up as S::visit::2. I kept per-visit families but a reached call continues the single open family (no completed member, a running or failed member), found by lineage. Several open families fail closed unless exactly one holds a running member. The target id is used only for fresh frames and the completed-collision check. I rejected both mapping-order selection and one global lineage per boundary (that would reject legitimate goto-retry histories). This reading is in specs/state.md and the plan.
- Frames whose id has no valid own suffix share one family, so two stale frames stay ambiguous instead of hiding as singletons.
- Missing loop-frame rows are tolerated by the repeat_until terminal checks, because an existing restore test deliberately drops that row; a present row must still match.
